head: This tail learned its fourth watched cue in a fifth of its control’s updates
sub:
Question: does each watched cue a Qwen3-8B tail learns make the next one cheaper, so the fourth cue costs at most 0.55 of the training?
Answer: {status_word}. Fourth cue, all 5 seeds: {RD_ctrl} of the updates of same-training controls (seed-level 95%: {RD_ctrl_lo} to {RD_ctrl_hi}); {RD_fresh} of fresh tails. Cheaper than both predictions.
setup: Reward takes a point off a praise opener like “Great question!”, but only when a cue is on: a small vector added inside the model, standing in for a sign that a grader is watching. The tail (last 2 of 36 layers) learns four cues in a row, each at right angles to the earlier ones. Learned = praise openers 10 points rarer with the cue on.
chart_title: Seed {seed}: RL updates to learn each new cue
key_chain: tail that learned the earlier cues
key_ctrl: control: same earlier updates, no earlier cue
ex_title: This prompt, after {t} updates on cue D: chance of a praise opener
note: Same prompt, same {t} updates: only the tail that learned three cues first already reacts to cue D.
foot: Source: Qwen3-8B, last 2 of 36 layers trained by reward (LoRA); 5 seeds per group; checked every 8 updates on 64 held-out prompts; Nov 2026 · athanorscience.com
